assumptions: Web discovery and entity validation are based on public web pages and primary sources; English-language search is accepted for v1.
At most 15 qualified opportunities; empty or smaller sets are valid when evidence is lacking, and results are never padded to reach 15.

Run success requires verified canonical URLs, audience fit evidence, activity or schedule freshness, explicit verified engagement mechanisms or actionable opportunities, and actual source URLs in the Evidence column.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session uses the existing pinned model pricing and spending ceiling (isolated profile, 900 seconds timeout).
Web search volume depends on audience specificity, niche community density, and URL verification passes.
Single markdown report output in reports/AUDIENCE_PROSPECTS.md up to 64,000 bytes.
effects: Writes one artifact reports/AUDIENCE_PROSPECTS.md to project state.
Read-only web search and page retrieval; no messages sent, no outreach executed, no external publishing, and no provider state mutated.

cases.description: Undergraduate CS students targeted via hackathons and university developer organizations with explicit sponsor/mentor routes.

inputs.target_audience: Undergraduate computer science and engineering students participating in student-led hackathons and developer clubs.
inputs.constraints: Focus on university-affiliated events and official student chapters; no unmoderated random forums.

contains: | Entity | Type | Verified URL | Audience Fit | Activity/Scale Evidence | Verified Engagement Mechanism | Evidence |

cases.description: Platform and infrastructure engineers targeted through local meetups, subreddits, and open-source user groups.

inputs.target_audience: DevOps, SRE, and platform engineers managing cloud infrastructure and container workloads.
inputs.constraints: Exclude generic tech channels; require specific user groups or forums with verifiable active discussions or meetups.

contains: | Entity | Type | Verified URL | Audience Fit | Activity/Scale Evidence | Verified Engagement Mechanism | Evidence |

rubric.question: Are all identified prospects specific named entities (clubs, hackathons, user groups, newsletters) rather than broad generic platforms?

Is every prospect backed by a verified canonical URL, explicit audience fit evidence, observable activity or confirmed schedule dates, and actual source URLs in the Evidence column supporting all claims?

Does each opportunity define an explicit, verified engagement mechanism or an upcoming/current/recurring actionable opportunity supported by source evidence, rather than inferred or speculative arrangements?
Are member counts, scale metrics, and activity claims grounded in source evidence, with unknown metrics marked Unknown and zero fabricated contacts?
Is the total number of qualified opportunities capped at 15 without padding, and are unpromising entities properly excluded or listed under disqualified?
